summary: Reproduced mixed tensor/list logprob normalization crashes in both scheduler consumers and guarded all six conversions with torch.is_tensor, preserving host list placeholders.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the source change, the real move_logprobs_to_cpu and _normalize_decode_outputs methods each raised AttributeError for mixed token-ID and mixed top-logprob entries on gfx950; exceptions were recorded per case.
Four regression and boundary tests passed after the fix, covering both consumers, all three affected fields, host lists, and tensor/empty-tensor entries.
11 tests and 2 subtests passed, including the focused regression and neighboring batch-result processor coverage.
All applicable formatting, lint, safety, and registered-test checks passed.
On AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950, mixed GPU tensors and host lists normalized exactly to the independently specified nested-list values and indices.

A real tiny-Llama SGLang server handled eight concurrent scored/plain request pairs (HTTP 200, eight tokens per response), logged a two-request decode batch, remained healthy, and was reaped by the subreaper runner.

gpu_evidence: Direct before/after conversion ran on AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950, and the tiny-Llama server log records ROCm engine execution plus a decode batch with two running requests; see reports/j-355548aa4ab4/raw/.
remaining_limitations: No production Qwen3.5-9B-derived weights were available; the deterministic random tiny Llama validates transport and engine execution only, not semantic or architecture-specific behavior.
The assigned hardware was AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950, not the reported NVIDIA B200/CUDA environment.
No multi-node or distributed workload was tested.
The HTTP fixture demonstrated mixed decode batching; the prefill-result consumer was covered directly with the real method rather than a separate prefill-only HTTP batch.
